title: Schedule 3 Dividends Paid Checker | Did a Dividend Move
content:
Schedules

Schedule 3 Dividends Paid Checker

Schedule 3 reports dividends paid and dividends received. A dividend either way means the year is not nil.

Three answersDividends onlyDeclared still countsEnds the nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Dividends in the tax year

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 3 Reports

Schedule 3 is where dividends go. Taxable dividends the corporation paid out during the year sit on one side of it, dividends it received from another corporation on the other, and it is where Part IV tax on a dividend from a connected corporation is worked out.

It is not a GIFI schedule, so nothing on the balance sheet brings it into play. The only question is whether a dividend moved. The guide to T2 schedules on a nil return sets out the schedules that are decided the other way, by what the corporation holds rather than by what it did.

The Three Things That Put a Year on It

What happenedWhere it landsIs the year still nil
A taxable dividend paid to a shareholderTaxable dividends paid, on Schedule 3No
A dividend received from another corporationDividends received, on Schedule 3No
A dividend declared and left unpaidStill a dividend, and still reportedNo
No dividend of any kindSchedule 3 has nothing to reportYes, on this question

The third row is the one owners get wrong. A declared dividend is activity whether or not any cash left the account, and the declaration is what counts rather than the payment.

Why a Dividend Ends the Nil Year

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

So this page has a short answer and a long one. The short answer is which part of Schedule 3 your year reaches. The long answer is that reaching any part of it settles a different question: the year is not nil, and nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year is for years that are. A holding corporation that pays or receives dividends is the ordinary case.

A schedule applying is not always a verdict on the whole year. This one is, because what puts a year on it is a dividend.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a dividend paid in cash differ from one declared?

Not for this purpose. A declared dividend is reported whether or not the cash has moved, so declaring one in a year the account never changed still puts the year on Schedule 3.

My corporation received a dividend and did nothing else. Is the year nil?

No. A dividend received is income, so the year is not nil however quiet the rest of it was.

Is Schedule 3 part of nil T2 filing?

The schedule is not the issue. A year that reaches Schedule 3 is not a nil year, and nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year is for years that are.

What is Part IV tax doing on this schedule?

Part IV tax can arise on a dividend received from a connected corporation, and Schedule 3 is where that calculation sits. It is another reason the schedule is not a formality.

Does a dividend between my own two corporations count?

Yes, on both returns. One paid it and one received it, so each of them reports its own side of the same dividend.

Is a shareholder loan repayment a dividend?

No. A loan repayment moves money that was already owed. Whether it is reported elsewhere is a separate question from this one.

Does a return of capital go on Schedule 3?

A return of capital is not a taxable dividend. If that is what happened, the question to settle first is what was actually resolved and recorded.

I paid myself a salary, not a dividend.

Then Schedule 3 has nothing to report on that account. A salary is payroll rather than a dividend, and it carries its own filings.

The dividend was in a year I have not filed yet.

It belongs to the year it was declared in, and that year is not nil. Each year stands on its own facts.

Nothing happened at all. Do I still file a schedule?

Not this one. Schedule 3 is driven by a dividend, and with none there is nothing for it to report. What the corporation holds still decides the GIFI schedules.

title: Schedule 7 Investment Income Calculator | What Totals Up
content:
Schedules

Schedule 7 Investment Income Calculator

Schedule 7 is where a private corporation totals its investment income. Any amount above nil means the year is not nil.

Three amounts inTotals what you enterInterest countsEnds the nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Investment income in the tax year

Enter the amounts above. Enter 0 where there was none.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 7 Does

Schedule 7 is where a private corporation totals its investment income: interest, rent, and the other passive amounts that arrive without anybody trading. It is the schedule that separates money the corporation earned from money it worked for.

For a dormant corporation it matters out of all proportion to the amounts involved, because the amounts are usually tiny and the consequence is not. Interest of a few dollars credited on a bank balance is investment income, and the year stops being nil.

What Totals Up, and What It Costs the Year

SourceCounts as investment incomeEffect on a nil year
Interest credited on a bank balanceYesThe year is not nil, whatever the amount
Rent received on a propertyYesA rental corporation is not nil
Other passive incomeYesThe year is not nil
Nothing credited at allNoNil on this question; what the corporation holds decides the GIFI schedules

There is no small-amount exception on this list. A balance that earned $12.00 across the year earned investment income, and that is the whole of the test.

Why Any Amount Ends the Nil Year

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

The calculator above adds up what you type and nothing else. It holds no rate, no threshold and no figure of ours: every amount in the result is one you entered. What it does is apply the test to the total, so a year with $12.00 of interest gets the same answer as a year with $12,000.00. See what nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers and the guide to filing for an inactive holding company.

Not every schedule settles whether a year is nil. This one does, and it settles it on any amount above zero.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a few dollars of bank interest really enough?

Yes. Interest credited on a balance is investment income, and the corporation is not nil for that tax year. The amount changes nothing about the test.

Where does the calculator get its figures?

From you. It totals the three amounts you enter and applies the test to the total. It holds no rate and no threshold of its own.

My bank paid interest but I never withdrew it.

Credited is enough. The income arose when it was credited to the account, whether or not anybody moved it afterwards.

Is rent from one property enough to end the nil year?

Yes. A rental corporation is not nil, and one property is a rental corporation for this purpose.

What if the interest was credited in a year I have not filed?

It belongs to that year, and that year is not nil. Each tax year is tested on its own facts.

Does a capital gain go here?

A gain is not the same thing as the interest and rent this page asks about. Either way a year with a gain in it is not a nil year.

My corporation holds shares that paid nothing.

Then nothing was credited and there is nothing to total. Holding an investment is not the same as earning from it.

Does this tell me what tax is owed?

No. It totals investment income and says what that means for the nil question. It works out no tax and is not a filed return.

The amounts are in a foreign currency.

Enter the figures you will report, in the currency the return uses. The conversion is a question for whoever prepares the return.

Everything is 0. What now?

Then this question leaves the year nil, and what the corporation holds decides the GIFI schedules instead. Share capital, cash, a shareholder loan, an incorporation cost or a bank charge each make them required.

title: Schedule 9 Related Corporations Checker | Not Schedule 50
content:
Schedules

Schedule 9 Related Corporations Checker

Schedule 9 reports related and associated corporations. It reaches a dormant corporation and does not end a nil year.

Three answersRelationships, not incomeReaches a dormant yearStill a nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

Corporate relationships

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 9 Reports, and What Schedule 50 Does Not

Schedule 9 reports the corporations yours is related to or associated with. It is a map of the group, and it is filed because the group exists rather than because anything happened in it.

It is routinely confused with Schedule 50, and the confusion runs one way: an owner who has filed Schedule 50 assumes the relationships are covered. They are not. Schedule 50 is not the schedule that reports related or associated corporations. It lists shareholders at 10% or more, which is a question about who owns this corporation rather than about which corporations stand beside it.

Two Questions That Look Like One

ScheduleWhat it reportsDecided by
Schedule 9Related and associated corporationsWhether a corporate relationship exists
Schedule 50Shareholders at 10% or moreWho holds the shares of this corporation
Schedule 24Shareholders and related corporations, onceWhether this is the first return after incorporation
Schedule 3Dividends paid and receivedWhether a dividend moved in the year

A single shareholder who owns two corporations outright triggers all of the first two: each corporation reports the other on its Schedule 9, and each reports that shareholder on its Schedule 50.

A Dormant Year Still Reports It

This is the page in the set that does not end a nil year. A relationship is reported whether or not either corporation traded, so a dormant corporation sitting in a group files the schedule and stays nil. Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers a year like that.

The reason is the same one the guide to T2 schedules on a nil return gives for the rest of them: what decides a schedule is not the amount of income, which is $0.00 on every nil return, but what the corporation holds, who owns it, and whether this is its first return. A relationship is in the same family of facts.

So this is the schedule that shows the rule is not uniform: it applies to the year and the year stays nil.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Schedule 9 the same as Schedule 50?

No, and this is the most common mix-up on a nil return. Schedule 50 lists shareholders at 10% or more. Schedule 9 reports the corporations yours is related to or associated with.

My corporation did nothing. Does it still report the relationship?

Yes. The relationship exists whether or not either corporation traded, and the schedule reports its existence.

Does filing Schedule 9 mean the year is not nil?

No. This is the one schedule in this set that leaves a nil year nil. It reports a connection, not income.

I own two corporations personally. Are they related?

Common ownership is exactly the kind of fact these questions turn on. Where the answer is yes, each corporation reports the other.

What is the difference between related and associated?

They are two separate tests, which is why the schedule and this page ask them separately. A corporation can meet one and not the other.

One of the two corporations is dissolved.

Then the question is what was true during the tax year being filed. A relationship that existed in that year is reported on that year.

Is this the same as Schedule 24?

No. Schedule 24 is filed once, on the first return after incorporation, and reports how the corporation came into existence. Schedule 9 is not a one-off.

Does a shareholder loan between the two change this?

It is a separate matter. A balance owed either way is reported where balances are reported; the relationship is reported here.

My corporations are in different provinces.

The relationship is still a relationship. Where each corporation is registered affects its registry filings, not this schedule.

Nothing is related or associated. Do I file a blank one?

There is nothing for it to report, so the question falls away. What the corporation holds still decides the GIFI schedules.

title: Schedule 23 Association Agreement Checker | Who Allocates
content:
Schedules

Schedule 23 Association Agreement Checker

Schedule 23 allocates the business limit between associated corporations. A nil year has no active business income to claim.

Three answersAssociated groupsNeeds active incomeA nil year is outside it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

The group and the year

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 23 Allocates

Associated corporations do not each get their own business limit for the small business deduction. They share one between them, and Schedule 23 is the agreement that says who takes what share of it.

Which means the schedule has two conditions before it means anything, and a dormant corporation fails the second. There has to be a group, and there has to be active business income to claim the deduction against. A nil year has none.

Who It Reaches, and Who It Does Not

The corporationAssociatedActive business incomeSchedule 23 in issue
An operating corporation in a groupYesYesYes
A dormant corporation in the same groupYesNoNo
A corporation that stands aloneNoYesNo
A dormant corporation standing aloneNoNoNo

The second row is the one that brings owners here. Being associated feels like it must create a filing, and on this schedule it does not: the allocation belongs to whichever corporation in the group has income to claim against.

Why a Nil Year Sits Outside It

A nil year has no active business income, so there is no small business deduction to claim, so there is no share of a limit to agree. The chain breaks at the first link and nothing downstream of it applies.

Being associated still matters elsewhere, and the mistake to avoid is reading this page as saying it does not. The relationship itself is reported on Schedule 9, which does reach a dormant corporation. What the dormant corporation is outside is the allocation, not the group. Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the dormant years either way.

Sitting inside a group and sitting outside this schedule are both true at once, and for a dormant corporation that is the ordinary position.

Frequently Asked Questions

My corporations are associated. Do I file Schedule 23?

Only where there is a business limit to allocate, which needs active business income and a small business deduction claim. A dormant corporation has neither.

Does being associated stop the year being nil?

No. Association is a relationship, and a relationship is not income. The year is tested on what the corporation did.

Which corporation files the agreement?

The allocation belongs with the corporations that have income to claim against. A dormant member of the group has no share to take.

What is the business limit?

It is the amount of active business income the small business deduction can be claimed on, and associated corporations share one between them rather than each having their own.

Is this the same as Schedule 9?

No. Schedule 9 reports that the relationship exists. Schedule 23 divides a limit between corporations that have income to apply it to.

My operating corporation claims the deduction and the holding company does not.

Then the allocation is a question on the operating corporation. The dormant or holding side has nothing to allocate.

Does a nil corporation reduce the limit for the others?

A corporation with no active business income has no claim to make. What the group agrees is a matter for the corporations making claims.

We never signed anything.

Then what is actually agreed is the question to settle, and it is a question for whoever prepares the return of the corporation claiming the deduction.

Does this page tell me the amount?

No. It tells you whether the question reaches your corporation at all. It calculates no limit and is not a filed return.

The corporation was dormant all year but associated. What do I file?

Not this. The relationship goes on Schedule 9, and what the corporation holds decides the GIFI schedules. The allocation does not arise.

title: Schedule 88 Internet Activities Checker | Parked or Earning
content:
Schedules

Schedule 88 Internet Activities Checker

Schedule 88 reports income earned from web pages and websites. A parked domain that earns nothing is outside it.

Three answersIncome, not hostingA parked domain is outsideEarning ends the nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

The corporation and its site

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 88 Actually Asks

Schedule 88 reports income earned from web pages and websites. The operative word is earned: the schedule follows the income, not the hosting bill and not the domain registration.

That distinction is the whole page, because a dormant corporation very often still has a site. The company that stopped trading in 2019 frequently still owns the domain, and the page is often still up. Neither fact is what this schedule asks about.

A Parked Domain and an Earning Site

What the corporation hasIncome through itSchedule 88Is the year still nil
A domain registered and nothing elseNoneNoYes, on this question
A page still up from when it tradedNoneNoYes, on this question
A page taking ordersYesYesNo
A site earning from advertising or affiliatesYesYesNo

The middle rows are where a dormant corporation usually sits. A page that has not been touched in four years earns nothing, and a schedule about income earned has nothing to take from it.

When a Site Ends the Nil Year

Income earned online is income. A corporation that took a single order through a page it had forgotten about had revenue that year, and the year is not nil, however dormant everything else was.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Where nothing came through the site, nothing here disqualifies the year, and nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers it. What the corporation holds still decides the GIFI schedules, which the guide to T2 schedules on a nil return sets out in full.

Having a site is not a verdict on the year. What came through it is.

Frequently Asked Questions

My corporation owns a domain but the site is blank.

Then nothing was earned through it and Schedule 88 has nothing to report. Owning a domain is not earning from one.

The old site is still up from when we traded. Does that count?

Not on its own. A page that earns nothing is outside a schedule about income earned from a page.

We took one small order online.

Then income arrived through the site, and the year is not nil. The size of the order does not change the test.

Does advertising revenue on a site count?

Income earned from a web page is what the schedule reports, whichever way the page earned it.

I pay for hosting every month. Is that reportable here?

A hosting cost is an expense, not income earned from the site. It belongs where expenses belong, and it does not bring this schedule into play.

Does a social media page count as a website?

The question the schedule asks is whether income was earned through a page. Where it was, the platform it sat on is not the deciding factor.

How many sites do I have to report?

The schedule asks about the pages that earned income. Pages that earned nothing are not what it is asking after.

Our site only has a contact form.

A form that generates no income earns nothing. If work came in through it and was paid for, that income is the point, not the form.

Does this affect GST/HST?

It is a separate account with separate filings. This page is about one schedule of the corporate return.

Nothing came through the site. What decides the schedules then?

What the corporation holds, who owns it, and whether this is its first return. Income is $0.00 on every nil return, so income is never what decides them.
